consumer: The frontend tile/sprite renderer reading the snapshot to draw each visible monster, asking 'what threat color should this monster be tinted?' — a value the engine SHOWS, not one any engine condition/mission/eligibility check evaluates.
scope: Per-visible-monster on the current view — a display proxy reach, not an inventory or predicate scope.
decisive_source: The engine's monster-attitude/threat-to-color display routine (the GUI's threat-tinting mapping) is NOT shown in the excerpts; Excerpts 1-2 (raw avatar/monster scalar getters) and Excerpt 3 (Creature::sees visibility predicate) are distractors that hold raw state or compute a different predicate, none mapping threat to a displayed color.
divergence: A monster whose raw attitude would naively map to red, but the GUI's display filter shows it differently (e.g. a remembered/half-visible shading or a clamped threat tint) — recomputing the color from raw state yields a different color than the engine would actually DISPLAY, exposing that raw state is not the display proxy.
